facts.label: official
facts.text: The Reserve Bank of India decided to conduct an overnight Variable Rate Repo auction for a notified amount of 50,000 crore INR on October 21, 2026.

facts.label: official
facts.text: The tenor of the overnight Variable Rate Repo auction scheduled by the central bank is 1 day.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: On Monday, the RBI announced a Rs 1-lakh-crore variable rate repo (VRR) auction for the first time since late July after the weighted average call rate (WACR) at 5.67% on Monday, or 17 basis points higher than the repo rate of 5.50%.
facts.text: The Reserve Bank of India announced a 1 lakh crore INR variable rate repo auction on Monday to ease banking liquidity ahead of the festive season.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: On Monday, the RBI announced a Rs 1-lakh-crore variable rate repo (VRR) auction for the first time since late July after the weighted average call rate (WACR) at 5.67% on Monday, or 17 basis points higher than the repo rate of 5.50%.
facts.text: The weighted average call rate climbed to 5.67 percent, exceeding the policy repo rate.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: RBI's VRR operation attracted bids of Rs 1.50 lakh crore while the banking system liquidity stood at a surplus of Rs 1.99 lakh crore as of October 16.
facts.text: Surplus liquidity across the banking system stood at 1.99 lakh crore INR as of October 16, 2026.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points on 7 October, from 5.25% to 5.5% (100 basis points make up one percentage point).
facts.text: The Reserve Bank of India raised the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points from 5.25 percent to 5.50 percent in its October policy decision.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: RBI data shows 68.2% of floating-rate loans are externally benchmarked.
facts.text: External benchmark lending rates are linked to 68.2 percent of outstanding floating-rate loans, allowing policy rate changes to swiftly transmit to retail borrowers.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: Monga estimates that a 25-basis-point increase would raise the monthly equated monthly instalment (EMI) on a ₹50 lakh home loan with a 30-year tenure by ₹852 at a public sector bank, from ₹34,109 to ₹34,961.
facts.text: A 25-basis-point increase in the benchmark repo rate is estimated to raise the monthly EMI on a 50 lakh INR 30-year home loan at a public sector bank by 852 INR.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: At a private bank, the EMI would rise by ₹867, from ₹35,821 to ₹36,688.
facts.text: At a private sector bank, the monthly EMI on a 50 lakh INR 30-year home loan is projected to rise by 867 INR following the rate increase.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: “We expect cumulative rate hikes by the central bank to the tune of another 50-75 bps over the next few months.
facts.text: Economists project cumulative policy rate hikes of another 50 to 75 basis points by the central bank over the coming months.

topic.summary: On a review of current and evolving liquidity conditions in the near term, it has been decided to conduct a Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, as under:                         Sl. No.          Notified Amount(₹ crore)          Tenor          (day)          Window Timing          Date of Reversal                          1          50,000          1          09:30 AM to 10:00 AM          October 22, 2026          (Thursday)                    2. The operational guidelines for the auction will be same as given in Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2021-2022/1572 dated January 20, 2022.      Ajit Prasad                  Deputy General Manager        (Communications)          Press Release: 2026-2027/1355
